48.0.s.en: 1. In praise of the prophet Elijah

48.0.0.en: 1 And Elijah the prophet stood up as fire, and his word burned like a torch. 2 He brought a famine upon them, and by his zeal he made them few in number. 3 By the word of the Lord he shut up the heaven, and brought down fire from it three times. 4 How glorious wast thou, O Elijah, in thy wondrous deeds! And who hath glory like unto thee? 5 Thou who didst raise up a dead man from death, and from hell, by the word of the Most High. 6 Who broughtest kings down to destruction, and the proud ones from their beds. 7 Thou who heardest the judgment in Sinai, and in Horeb the sentences of vengeance. 8 Who anointedst kings for vengeance, and prophets to succeed after thee. 9 Who wast taken up in a whirlwind of fire, in a chariot of fiery horses. 10 Who wast ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath before it break forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father unto the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob. 11 Blessed are they that saw thee, and they that have obtained the glory of thy friendship. 12 For we shall live this life, but after death we shall not have such a name.

48.0.1.en: Then stood up Elijah the prophet as fire, and his word was kindled like a lamp [1].

48.0.2.en: Ben Sira highlighted what marked the prophet Elijah, the man of faith: a fiery heart kindled with zeal for the word of God and for worship of Him, not of idols; therefore it was said of him: Elijah the prophet stood up as fire to burn up evil, stubbornness and resistance to God, especially on the part of King Ahab and his wife Jezebel. And at the same time his word was kindled like a lamp that enlightens the souls longing for the truth in the midst of the pitch darkness of corruption. Elijah was a great prophet, although in human weakness he feared the wicked queen Jezebel, who dominated the personality of her husband King Ahab and corrupted his faith, and killed many of the prophets (1 Kgs 18-19), and at the same time Ahab and Jezebel were in great terror of him.

48.0.3.en: It is said of the angels that they are God's servants, burning with the fire of holy zeal (Ps 104:4); Elijah imitated them, so he brought down fire three times (2 Kgs 1:10-14), and was taken up to heaven in a chariot of fiery horses (2 Kgs 2:11). Elijah did not die, and his coming is awaited together with Enoch, to resist the antichrist and support the believers at that time.

48.1.0.en: It is he who brought a famine upon them, and by his zeal made them few in number [2].

48.2.0.en: By the word of the Lord he shut up the heaven, and brought down fire three times [3].

48.2.1.en: If sin has corrupted our life and made of us a land that brings forth thorns and thistles (Gen 3:18), then we have become in need of the word of God, the consuming fire, to burn up these thorns and thistles.

48.2.2.en: v In truth there are thorns that are not scattered, but are in the hands of the one who is drunk with vice and are driven deep into it, so that the person forgets his sobriety, and as it is said in the Proverbs, "thorns hidden in the hands of the drunkard" (see Prov 26:9).

48.2.3.en: Must we not speak words describing any disturbances that sow evils which afflict the one who receives them in the very being of his soul? He who receives deep moral evil in his soul, so that it becomes a land that brings forth thorns (Gen 3:18), needs the word of the living God to cut it off from its roots, which is more terrible and sharper than a two-edged sword, and hotter than fire [1].

48.2.4.en: v He who adds evil in the depths of his soul until it becomes a land that brings forth thorns needs to have this cut off by the living and active word of God, which is sharper than any two-edged sword and more able than any fire to burn (Heb 4:12; Sir 48:1). That fire which exposes the thorns, and which by its divinity stops them! So the threshing floors and the fields of wheat have no need of (another) fire to be sent to such a soul [2].

48.2.5.en: Origen: By your wonders you were honored, O Elijah! And who can glory like you [3]? [4]

48.2.6.en: v Who will make room for my word to tell his beauty (the beauty of Elijah) from his childhood, in what life he was brought up?

48.2.7.en: Who will give me a book to help me look and see how radiant with holiness he was from his youth?

48.2.8.en: His lofty and spiritual beauty is hidden from me; how did he begin to walk on his way toward God?

48.2.9.en: Scripture showed his story to the world only here, when he withheld the rain and the dew because of Ahab (1 Kgs 17:1).

48.2.10.en: Up to here the way of his righteousness and the beauty of his conduct and the excellence of his virginity were hidden.

48.2.11.en: From here Scripture began to relate his story, because on account of the iniquity of Ahab he bound the heaven with one word.

48.2.12.en: You, then, consider from before this great work, how many were his works and labors for the sake of God?

48.2.13.en: And therefore Scripture hid his life, because it was lofty, and we could not speak of it.

48.2.14.en: From his childhood he held fast to a great way of life, with victorious works, such that even nature could not bear them.

48.2.15.en: As soon as he knew the difference between good and evil, he began with the good, and evil never overcame him.

48.2.16.en: As soon as he knew the world, he left it lest he live in it, and loved the wilderness and dwelling alone on the mountains.

48.2.17.en: And as soon as he felt that there was another world of God, he set his face toward it, running to reach it.

48.2.18.en: As soon as he saw that this world is passing away, he did not stoop to its company, nor to work in it.

48.2.19.en: As soon as he heard that this place was not his place, he no longer loved it, and did not wish to come near its deeds.

48.2.20.en: From the time he knew that there is another life of God, he sought for it with great labors in order to inherit it.

48.2.21.en: As soon as he understood that Adam died when he transgressed the commandment, he did not turn aside from the spiritual law.

48.2.22.en: He looked at (human) nature (and understood) that if it had not sinned it would not have died, so he was terrified of sin, lest he become a fruit of death.

48.2.23.en: Since he knew what death is and what life is, he wrestled for life so as to acquire it.

48.2.24.en: From his youth he was brought up spiritually toward the great height until he reached this rank, the highest of all.

48.3.0.en: He looked to God, and as soon as he knew how beautiful He is, he no longer turned his gaze away from Him to see anything (else) [4].

48.4.0.en: St. Jacob of Serugh: You raised a dead man from death, and from Hades by the word of the Most High [5].

48.4.1.en: The prophet Elijah raised the son of the widow of Zarephath, the Gentile woman (1 Kgs 17:1-24). Elijah stretched himself upon the dead child three times, crying to the Most High to restore the child's life; this points to his taking refuge in the Holy Trinity, the Giver of life.

48.4.2.en: v The widow's son died, because the son of the Church, that is, the Gentiles, died because of their many sins and transgressions.

48.4.3.en: Through the prayers of Elijah the widow's son recovered life; and by the coming of Christ the son of the Church, that is, the Christian people, came out of the prison of death.

48.4.4.en: Elijah bowed down in prayer, and the widow's son recovered life. So Christ plunged into His sufferings, and the Christian people recovered life. Why did Elijah bow down three times to raise the boy?.. In truth he bowed down three times, showing the mystery of the Trinity. The whole Trinity restored life to the widow's son, or to the Gentiles. Moreover, this is fulfilled in the sacrament of Baptism, where the old man is immersed in the water three times so that the new man may be made worthy to rise [5].

48.5.0.en: St. Augustine: And you brought down kings to destruction, and those who were glorified from their beds [6].

48.5.1.en: v The Lord called His righteous servant and spoke with him: Arise, go down to meet Ahab the king (1 Kgs 21:17-18), and expose his lie.

48.5.2.en: Behold, he has gone down to inherit the seized vineyard. Go and tell him: You shall not enjoy an inheritance that is not your own.

48.5.3.en: Go and tell this one who killed and thought he had inherited: Naboth has handed his vineyard over to Me, and he is dying.

48.5.4.en: I, I am the heir of that meek one, and the vineyard is My possession, and I stand over his inheritance, and I execute his judgment.

48.5.5.en: What do you want from the possession handed over into My hands? He called upon Me as he was being stoned and commanded me, and I will not neglect it.

48.5.6.en: I demand justice to avenge Naboth and every wronged one, for his judgment is kept for Me, and I will not keep silent.

48.5.7.en: In the place where the dogs licked his blood they shall lick your blood (1 Kgs 21:19); behold, you are repaid with the measure of blood with which you also measured (Mt 7:2)...

48.5.8.en: He goes forward boldly to drive the king from the inheritance, armed with the Lord, and he takes no account of the kings of the earth.

48.5.9.en: And righteousness and uprightness follow him, and faith and perfection run with him (Ps 85:10-11).

48.5.10.en: He despised the crown, because the smell of iniquity rose from it, and he made light of authority greatly without fear.

48.5.11.en: And as Ahab was standing in the vineyard which he had gone down to inherit, he saw Elijah coming, and the wicked one trembled.

48.5.12.en: The prophet met the king like the thief and the master of the house, and the plunder was not hidden.

48.5.13.en: He caught him in a vineyard whose owner had been killed on his account, and the king was ashamed before the sight of the blood he had shed.

48.5.14.en: The king said: "Hast thou found me, O mine enemy?" (1 Kgs 21:20). He was indeed the enemy of the house of God and of the prophet.

48.5.15.en: The partner of the idols and of the gods of the Amorites showed himself how he hated the servants of the Lord.

48.5.16.en: There was great enmity between him and the Lord, because he was a friend of all the gods of the Canaanites.

48.5.17.en: And as the prophet stood before him rebuking him, he was his enemy, as he called him and exposed himself.

48.5.18.en: The righteous one said: Yes, I have found you as you said, for you cannot hide your iniquity from the Lord.

48.5.19.en: Your hands are full of innocent blood, so how will you be justified? Seizure and plunder are within your gate, so how will you escape?

48.5.20.en: The house of its planner Jezebel cannot stand; you have taken possession of the inheritance by blood, so how will you be saved?

48.5.21.en: The Lord searches out your iniquity, and exposes you, and holds you accountable for murder and plunder and all evils.

48.5.22.en: And in justice He will destroy your dwelling filled with iniquity, and will take vengeance on you in uprightness, because you have provoked Him [6].

48.5.23.en: St. Jacob of Serugh: Fiery Elijah and King Ahaziah (2 Kgs 1): Ahaziah the son of Ahab and Jezebel heard about his parents, whose blood the dogs licked, because they had turned aside from the way of truth. Now, since he did not benefit from the experience of his parents, just as discipline came upon his father so that the dogs licked his blood, the prophetic voice came to him: "Thou shalt not come down off that bed."

48.5.24.en: v The messengers of the son of Ahab heard from Elijah, and returned to him bearing bad news (2 Kgs 1:5).

48.5.25.en: They entered, and told him all they had heard from Elijah, and they repeated before him that he would not come down from his bed (2 Kgs 1:6).

48.5.26.en: They carried to this sick pagan the tidings of death, and wounded his heart with the word they had heard from Elijah...

48.5.27.en: He watched for opportunities to close the way of idolatry, lest the circumcised sons of Abraham walk in it.

48.5.28.en: He gathered them from every side to God, after they had been scattered among the idols of the Canaanites.

48.5.29.en: He brought them back from the strange ways, to walk in the great way of the King their Lord.

48.5.30.en: When they went out in the paths of the Amorites, the zealous one arose and brought them back to his God.

48.5.31.en: The flock of Isaac left the river of living water (Jer 2:13), to go and drink of the water of evil which destroys it.

48.5.32.en: Elijah, the good shepherd, drove it away (from there), lest it drink from the springs that spew forth death.

48.6.0.en: The poison of the serpent was in the river of the Canaanites, and (Elijah) watched every day lest the flock drink from it [7].

48.6.1.en: St. Jacob of Serugh: And you heard a rebuke in Sinai, and in Horeb sentences of vengeance [7].

48.6.2.en: Ahab told his wife Jezebel what Elijah had done, and how he had killed the priests of Baal, and she was greatly enraged and resolved to kill him. Elijah was compelled to flee to Beersheba which belongs to Judah, where an angel sustained him there. The Spirit led him to go to Mount Horeb, the mountain on which Moses received the Law (1 Kgs 19).

48.7.0.en: v After the preparation of forty days of fasting Elijah saw the Lord on Mount Horeb. And he heard from Him the words: "What doest thou here, Elijah?" Here the saying is very close to the saying: "Adam, where art thou?" in the Book of Genesis. The aim of the latter is to stir the fears of one who had eaten and was lost, while the former is addressed to a fasting servant with tenderness and love [8].

48.7.1.en: St. Jerome v The prophet walked in the wilderness forty days (1 Kgs 19:8), and reached Horeb, the mountain of the Lord, and settled there.

48.7.2.en: He walked and accomplished the way of perfection with diligence, and entered the place in which Moses was enlightened.

48.8.0.en: He lodged in a cave (1 Kgs 19:9), whose name and work were beloved, and it is preferred to him who dwells in it above the palace of kings [9].

48.8.1.en: St. Jacob of Serugh: You anointed kings for retribution, and prophets to minister after you [8].

48.8.2.en: The kings whom Elijah anointed are Hazael and Jehu, and as for the prophets, he anointed Elisha his disciple. And since it is recorded of Obadiah that he hid a hundred prophets from the slaughter ordered by Queen Jezebel, perhaps all these prophets or some of them were anointed by the prophet Elijah (1 Kgs 18:3-4).

48.8.3.en: You were taken up in a whirlwind of fire, in a chariot of fiery horses [9].

48.8.4.en: v Let us then speak of the ascent of this beautiful one, and of the splendid chariot which came down to him on the earth.

48.8.5.en: And of the fleshly one who was found worthy to dwell with the spiritual, and of the earthy one who did not return to the earth to become dust.

48.8.6.en: And of the lowly one who directed his way toward the heavenly ones, and of the son of our race who left us and mingled with the angels.

48.9.0.en: And of the wonder that seized the earth, because the heavenly ones snatched one from her bosom, to be with them among their choirs [10].

48.9.1.en: St. Jacob of Serugh: And you shall come to rebuke at the appointed time, as it is written, to pacify the wrath of God before its fury, and to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob [10].

48.9.2.en: The wisdom of the prophet Elijah declares that he acts in everything at the appropriate time.

48.10.0.en: Blessed are those who saw you, and those who have fallen asleep in love, for we also shall surely live (after death) [11].

48.10.1.en: v The union of the body with the soul prepares it to appear to the light out of the darkness of the womb. But the union of the soul with the body (its submission to it) confines it in the darkness of the body. Therefore we must not spare the body, but subdue it as an enemy of the soul and an adversary to it. For absorption in delicious foods stirs up evil passions, while a fasting stomach quiets the passions and rescues the soul [11].

48.11.s.en: 2. In praise of the prophet Elisha

48.11.0.en: 13 And Elijah was covered in the whirlwind; and Elisha was filled with his spirit, and in his days he was not moved for fear of any ruler, neither could any bring him under. 14 No word could overcome him, and after his death his body prophesied. 15 He did wonders in his life, and at his death his works were marvellous. 16 For all this the people repented not, neither departed they from their sins, till they were spoiled and carried out of their land, and were scattered through all the earth, 17 and there was left a small people, and a ruler in the house of David, 18 some of them did that which was pleasing, and some multiplied sins.

48.11.1.en: After the ascent of the prophet Elijah to heaven, the prophetic work was received by his disciple Elisha, who desired that two portions of his teacher's spirit might rest upon him so that he might fulfill his mission and face the growing tide of evil. God granted that there be accomplished at his hands double the miracles which his teacher had performed, to affirm the need of society for increased work because of the increase of corruption.

48.11.2.en: v O distinguished ones, listen to me, and I will speak further about the disciple who has amazed me by the beauty of his way.

48.11.3.en: His teacher (the prophet Elijah) overcame me, so I fell silent about him and did not describe him, and this one also stirs me by his wonder and his conduct.

48.11.4.en: Yes, in truth he is the disciple of that beautiful one, and his beauty springs from his deeds wherever he went.

48.11.5.en: He wrought a victory over the bad waters which he healed, and gave health to the sick and desolate land.

48.11.6.en: By his prophecy he put an end to death and restrained it, so it went out after seeing his might [12].

48.11.7.en: St. Jacob of Serugh: Elijah was covered by the whirlwind, and Elisha was filled with his spirit, and in his days he was not shaken or trembled before any ruler, and no one subdued [13] him [12].

48.11.8.en: The last scene in the life of the prophet Elijah reveals to us the depth of the tender feelings which Elisha held for his teacher. And as he realized that the end was near, he resolved to be with him to the end. Nothing could persuade him to leave Elijah, and when he asked him what he should do for him before he was taken from him, he asked for the portion of the firstborn son, a double portion of his teacher's spirit (2 Kgs 2:9). He saw his teacher in a terrifying sight, so he rent his clothes, and took up the mantle of his teacher, and returned to the Jordan, striking the water to see whether the spirit of Elijah had really rested upon him, and when the water was parted he crossed over on dry ground. By this the sons of the prophets who were watching the scene from the hills realized that the spirit of Elijah had rested on Elisha, so they bowed to him in respect and submission (2 Kgs 2:12-15). Here Elisha began his ministry which lasted about fifty years, for it extended throughout the reign of Jehoram and Jehu and Jehoahaz and Joash.

48.11.9.en: No word could overcome him, and even after the sleep of death his body prophesied [13].

48.12.0.en: He did wonders in his life, and even after his death his works were astonishing [14].

48.12.1.en: When the ten tribes (the northern kingdom) were split off and rebelled against God, and set up temples and altars and worship according to their own desire, He sent to them fiery Elijah and his disciple Elisha the prophet, the wonder-worker. Believers do not need to have wonders performed; rather they are given to unbelievers. The Apostle says: "Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to them that believe not: but prophesying (preaching) serveth not for them that believe not, but for them which believe" (1 Cor 14:22).

48.12.2.en: Elisha was a wonder-worker even after his death, for his dry bones raised a dead man who was cast into the grave (2 Kgs 13:21). The Lord allowed this miracle so that, when the people fell under captivity and counted themselves like the dead, they might know that God sends them one who will bring them back to the Promised Land. For the man of God is sanctified in all that is his, even his bones after his death. St. Augustine says that the prophecies did not stop at being declared by words, but were also given by symbolic acts [14] such as the raising of the dead man by the bones of Elisha.

48.12.3.en: v The prophets spoke of him in amazement (and said): The spirit of his teacher came upon him and overflowed (2 Kgs 2:15).

48.12.4.en: They asked him to heal, as from a spiritual physician, the sick (corrupt) and desolate land which was barren. They saw power in him, so they asked him to heal the bad waters, and to relieve the whole land by his proven virtue. They said to him: The village is good and its location beautiful, but the waters are bad and the land is desolate and distresses us (2 Kgs 2:19).

48.13.0.en: He said to them: Bring me a new cruse, and put salt therein; and they did as he said. He took it and went out to the spring, and cast the salt into the bad waters, and healed them because they were sick (2 Kgs 2:20-22) [15].

48.14.0.en: St. Jacob of Serugh: The prophet Elisha died, and was buried in the grave, and his body decayed, and nothing remained but a heap of dry bones. But these bones bear witness to the spirit of power which the prophet lived and which death could not crush. After the death of the prophet Elisha, when the raiders of Moab cast a man into his grave, and the corpse touched the bones of Elisha, he lived and stood up on his feet (2 Kgs 13:21). St. Ephrem the Syrian says: [None of the prophets after his death raised a man. Therefore we see that the spirit of Elijah rested doubled upon Elisha. In fact, the authority which the Lord gave to the bones of Elisha is a symbol and seed of the resurrection. And the honor that was given to them shows the glory which the bodies of the saints will have, being clothed with it on the day of the resurrection of all the dead [16].]

48.14.1.en: v The dust of the righteous, which was scattered in Hades upon the dust, is chosen gold, and a spring full of good things.

48.14.2.en: The pure body, which the lusts did not defile, is the dust of the righteous, and it is a treasure of relics in which there is tenderness for him who approaches it...

48.14.3.en: Every day a sweet fragrance rises spiritually from their bones, which no ointment resembles.

48.14.4.en: In their corpses the divine indwelling dwells like the Kingdom in a temple of gold and pearls.

48.14.5.en: From their bodies flows Gihon (Gen 2:13) for all the healings, which used to grow beside the tree of life (Gen 2:19)..

48.14.6.en: From the sinner a foul smell rises at his death, but the righteous man is the chosen censer of God...

48.15.0.en: He fell asleep in God, and behold, life awakens in him every day; he died to the world and became alive to his Lord, the joy of the face [17].

48.15.1.en: St. Jacob of Serugh: And with all this the people did not repent, nor did they cease from their sins, until their land was seized, and they were scattered in all the earth [15].

48.15.2.en: He speaks here of the Assyrian captivity of the kingdom of Israel, when the kingdom of Judah, small in number, remained, and the ruler of the house of David was Hezekiah king of Judah (2 Chr 30:1-12).

48.15.3.en: And there was left but a small remnant, and a ruler of the house of David.

48.15.4.en: Some of them did that which was good, and some multiplied sins [16].

48.15.5.en: By "some of them" he means those who did the virtues of King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah.

48.16.0.en: v Those who strive toward the virtuous life and the life of love for God are zealous toward (acquiring) the virtues of the Spirit as possessions whose ownership cannot be transferred to another, and which bring eternal rest. These use temporal things merely because they are necessary (and not out of luxury), and according to the will and providence of God, and they use them with joy and all gratitude, even if it be only enough for subsistence. For the lavish table feeds bodies, since they are material, but the knowledge of God, and victory over self, and goodness, and doing good to all, and compassion and meekness... these glorify the soul [18].

48.17.s.en: 3. In praise of King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah

48.17.0.en: 19 Hezekiah fortified his city, and brought in water into the midst thereof; he dug the rock with iron, and built wells for the water. 20 In his days Sennacherib came up, and sent Rabshakeh; and he came and lifted up his hand against Zion, and boasted in his pride. 21 Then trembled their hearts and hands, and they were in pain as women in travail. 22 But they called upon the merciful Lord, stretching out their hands toward Him; and the Holy One quickly heard them out of heaven, 23 and delivered them by the hand of Isaiah. 24 He smote the camp of the Assyrians, and His angel destroyed them. 25 For Hezekiah had done the thing that pleased the Lord, and was strong in the ways of David his father, which Isaiah the prophet commanded him, who was great and faithful in his vision. 26 In his days the sun went backward, and he lengthened the king's life. 27 He saw by an excellent spirit what should come to pass at the last, and he comforted them that mourned in Zion. 28 He showed what should come to pass for ever, and secret things or ever they came.

48.17.1.en: Hezekiah knew that his father was responsible for what had befallen the people because of his calling on Assyria to intervene in the politics of the Holy Land (2 Chr 28:16-21). He began the religious reform to repair what his father Ahaz had corrupted, and cleansed the Temple of idols. The Kingdom of God had priority in the life of King Hezekiah, with the renewal of spiritual wisdom.

48.17.2.en: Hezekiah dug a channel underground through a rock so that Jerusalem could obtain water secretly from the spring of Gihon. This heroic work is recorded twice in the Old Testament (2 Kgs 20:20; 2 Chr 32:30).

48.17.3.en: Hezekiah fortified his city, and brought the water into the midst of it, dug the hard rock with iron, and built cisterns for water [17].

48.17.4.en: Sirach begins with the rebellion of King Hezekiah against Assyria, for which he had prepared himself by fortifying Jerusalem, the capital of his kingdom, and digging a channel in solid rock so that the people might find water when Assyria laid siege to the city. This supported the city during the siege of Sennacherib in 701 BC [18-20].

48.17.5.en: In his days Sennacherib came up, and sent Rabshakeh and withdrew, then lifted up his hand against Zion, and boasted in his pride [18].

48.17.6.en: "Rabshakeh" [18] is an Assyrian title whose meaning is perhaps "chief of staff (a body of military officers)" or governor. Sennacherib king of Assyria encamped at Lachish and sent the arrogant Rabshakeh to besiege the city of Jerusalem and to demand of King Hezekiah that he hand the city over to him. But Hezekiah turned toward God in a spirit of repentance, and God sent him the prophet Isaiah to reassure him. The angel of the Lord killed 185,000 of the army of Sennacherib (2 Kgs 19:35).

48.17.7.en: Then their hearts and hands trembled, and they were in pain as women in travail [19].

48.18.0.en: And they called upon the merciful Lord, stretching out their hands toward Him, and the Holy One heard them quickly from heaven, and rescued them by the hand of Isaiah [20].

48.19.0.en: He smote the camp of the Assyrians, and His angel destroyed them [21].

48.19.1.en: v When you close the door of your dwelling and remain alone, know that you have with you an angel, appointed by God for every man, whom the Greeks call "the spirit of the house." He does not sleep, and sees everything by his constant accompanying of you, and is not deceived, and nothing is hidden from him in the darkness. And know that God is beside you, present in every place, for there is no place or space in which God is not present. He is greater than all and holds all in His hand [19].

48.20.0.en: St. Anthony the Great: For Hezekiah did that which pleased the Lord, and flourished in strength in the ways of David his father, which great Isaiah, faithful in his vision, commanded him [22].

48.21.0.en: In his days the sun went back, and he lengthened the life of the king [23].

48.21.1.en: The Lord gave Hezekiah a sign as he asked (2 Kgs 20:8), to confirm the fulfillment of the divine promise thus: the sun's going back ten degrees (Isa 38:8). Some see that it was merely the retreat of the shadow on the steps that lead to a "balcony" in the palace or that lead to the upper room. And some see that it was an eclipse of the sun that occurred on January 11, 689 BC. The sun is the true measure of time, and in the hand of God, the mover of history and events and time itself, He used it as a sign in the days of Joshua (Josh 10:12), and also in the days of Hezekiah, and when the Lord of glory was crucified, and before His final coming when the sun will be darkened.

48.21.2.en: And with a great spirit he saw the last things, and comforted [20] those who mourn in Zion [24].

48.21.3.en: The message of Isaiah was the revealing of the last times, to arouse in the people the spirit of hope, especially concerning the Incarnation of the Son of God and His offering Himself as a sacrifice of salvation. And the writers of the New Testament, such as St. Matthew the Evangelist, quoted much from the prophecies of Isaiah about the person of the Lord Christ and His life and His characteristics and His ministry, especially concerning the mystery of the Cross.

48.22.0.en: And he revealed what would be to the last times, and the hidden things before they came to pass [25].

48.22.1.en: The prophecies of the prophet Isaiah were distinguished not only by their multitude, but by their wonderful precision, especially the birth of the Lord Christ from a virgin, and the affirmation that He is the Mighty God, and details about the mystery of the Cross and its message.

48.22.2.en: The subject of the "Kingdom of God" with Isaiah is not only given priority over any other subject, but he counts it the main element in everything. He wishes to send every believer forth to see and understand the plan of God, not only in his own time but to the end of the ages.

48.22.3.en: In the view of the prophet Isaiah, the wise seer, the foundation of the believer's life is not the management of his temporal affairs, but that he be far-sighted. Not to be concerned with his needs through tens of years and the life of his children and grandchildren, but to gaze upon what happens until the end of the world and the passing over into the age to come.

48.23.s.en: By Your wisdom You raise up in every generation wise men who challenge the darkness!

48.23.0.en: v I praise You, O incarnate Wisdom of God, Giver of wisdom and discernment and strength and holiness.

48.23.1.en: By Your wisdom You sent fiery Elijah to challenge the killer of the prophets.

48.23.2.en: And by Your wisdom You sent Elisha, the wonder-worker, even in his grave his bones raised a dead man!

48.23.3.en: And by Your wisdom You raised up King Hezekiah, who did not flatter his father but demolished his idols!

48.23.4.en: And by Your wisdom You sent the prophet Isaiah to support the believers in the midst of corruption, that they might come to know the Savior of sinners.

48.23.5.en: v In every generation You send men of God, each suited to his time, to save all!

48.23.6.en: And with every believer You offer gifts and abilities by Your divine plan for the salvation of his own soul and his brethren.

48.23.7.en: My heart cries to You, saying: We praise You for Your wonderful works in every generation.

48.23.8.en: O Lord of the harvest, send laborers, for the harvest is plenteous, but the laborers are few.

48.23.9.en: Reveal to every believer his mission, for the edification of Your eternal Kingdom!

48.23.10.en: Grant us not to despise anyone, You who chose the foolish things of the world to confound the wise!

48.23.11.en: To You be glory, O You who are wonderful in Your wisdom and Your plan and Your power!
